content.value_statement: Tailwind CSS v4 projects need consistent responsive patterns and token choices. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concise guidance for CSS-first configuration, layout, theming, and performance.
actual_capabilities: Explains Tailwind v4 changes, including CSS-based theme configuration and Oxide.
Shows when to use viewport breakpoints versus container queries.
Lists mobile-first responsive prefixes and layout class patterns.
Provides dark mode strategy guidance for class, media, and selector approaches.
Outlines design token layers for primitive, semantic, and component values.
Identifies common Tailwind anti-patterns and performance considerations.
limitations: Does not install Tailwind packages or run build commands.
Does not inspect external documentation during use unless the agent chooses to search.
Does not replace project-specific design review or accessibility testing.
Guidance is focused on Tailwind CSS v4 and may not fit older v3 setups.

use_cases.title: Plan a Tailwind v4 Migration
use_cases.description: Identify which v3 configuration habits should move to CSS-first theme definitions and modern utility patterns.

use_cases.title: Define Design Tokens
use_cases.description: Create a clear token structure for colors, spacing, typography, and component-specific values.

use_cases.title: Improve Responsive Components
use_cases.description: Choose when components should use viewport breakpoints, container queries, or reusable extracted patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Learn v4 Basics
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of Tailwind v4 concepts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the main Tailwind CSS v4 changes in my project and recommend which patterns to adopt first.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Responsive Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component and suggest mobile-first Tailwind classes, container query usage, and dark mode variants.

prompt_templates.title: Build Token System
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Tailwind v4 CSS-first token structure for colors, spacing, typography, and component values.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Pattern Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Tailwind implementation for duplicated class lists, excessive arbitrary values, weak tokens, and performance issues. Recommend fixes by priority.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to modernize a Tailwind v3 setup.
output_examples.output: A migration outline that recommends CSS-first theme definitions, semantic tokens, limited directive use, and full v4 adoption.

output_examples.input: A component layout breaks when placed inside a narrow card.
output_examples.output: A recommendation to make the card a container, use container-based breakpoints, and keep page-level breakpoints for outer layout.

output_examples.input: A design system needs typography and color guidance.
output_examples.output: A token plan separating raw colors, semantic values, component tokens, font stacks, and type scale usage.

best_practices: Start with mobile styles, then add larger breakpoint variants only where layouts need them.
Use semantic design tokens before adding many arbitrary values.
Prefer reusable components when long utility combinations repeat across the interface.
anti_patterns: Mixing Tailwind v3 JavaScript configuration with a partial v4 CSS-first setup.
Using inline styles or important flags to solve normal specificity problems.
Adding template-generated class names that Tailwind cannot detect reliably.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands?
faq.answer: No. It is Markdown guidance, and it does not include executable scripts or command instructions.

faq.question: Is it specific to Tailwind CSS v4?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on Tailwind CSS v4, though some layout and token principles also help older projects.

faq.question: Can it help migrate from v3?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide migration decisions, but it does not perform automated migrations by itself.

faq.question: Does it generate complete UI components?
faq.answer: It can guide structure and class choices. Final component code still depends on your framework and project conventions.

faq.question: Does it cover accessibility?
faq.answer: It supports layout and theme decisions, but accessibility still needs dedicated review and testing.

faq.question: Why are container queries included?
faq.answer: Container queries help reusable components respond to parent width instead of only the viewport.
